title: Push-Stroke Line Technique
description: Players push the length of the court focusing purely on a long, full hand-rim stroke before the ball is ever introduced, building the propulsion technique every other skill depends on.

content.objective: Build a long, efficient push stroke with a full hand-rim follow-through, at a controlled pace.
content.setup: Players line up on the baseline in their chairs with the full length of the court open ahead.
instructions: Push the full length of the court using the longest stroke you can control.
Let the hand follow all the way through the rim before releasing for the recovery swing.
Keep the trunk stable and lean slightly forward into each stroke rather than rocking side to side.
Roll to a stop under control at the far end, then push back at an easy pace.
coachingPoints: A longer, fuller stroke beats a fast, short one — quality before speed.
Keep the elbows relaxed and let the push come from the shoulder and trunk, not just the wrist.
Release cleanly off the rim instead of dragging the hand.
commonMistakes: Short, choppy strokes that never reach full extension.
Rocking the trunk side to side instead of driving straight forward.
Gripping the rim too tightly, which slows the stroke down.
content.safety: Keep a clear lane ahead at all times and check for other groups before pushing at speed.
progressions: Add a stopwatch and count strokes needed to cross the court — fewer, longer strokes is the goal.
regressions: Shorten the distance to half court while the technique is still being learned.
variations: Push backward under control for the return trip to add a reverse-tracking challenge.
